correctness.rationale: The displayed integer generator has a rank-four identity block. The complete attached 9 all-equal and 36 two-pair coefficient bundles were replayed from actual files by verify.py; every coefficient is ±1, every sum equals its requested integer column and the four supports are pairwise disjoint. The 3+1 and 2+1+1 patterns require respectively three and two PIR bundles avoiding at most one and two singleton indices, and distinct requests use singleton sets; the verifier checked all 495 multisets. The exact integer identities hold over every finite field. Independently, the cited source Propositions 18 and 10(iii) yield the lower bound nine via eight-column three-request minimum. Limits: this proves neither unique optimality nor all possible target vectors.

originality.rationale: The full arXiv:2601.04041v2 source establishes the universal lower bound and the characteristic-two exact value, but its Theorem 23 gives only 9≤ASP(4,4,q)≤ASB(4,4,q)≤10 for odd q. Its existing nine-column single-parity construction is explicitly credited as equivalent to the present one; what is new is the all-odd-characteristic signed-integer recovery proof, not inventing that matrix. The strongest related exact published record concerns dimension three, and the paper’s dimension-five characteristic-three case does not imply an all-odd-field dimension-four optimum. The exact claim, aliases, four-cycle construction and other overlaps were queried, with the residual risk of unindexed prior work noted.
residual_risks: An unindexed prior note or an inaccessible unpublished exact finite-field classification might already imply the all-odd-field four-dimensional result.
The related dimension-three record could not be reviewed beyond its indexed abstract; it has different dimension and is not decisive for the present claim.
The exact result is only for four all-symbol stored-column requests, not for functional batch codes or other dimensions.

value.rationale: The primary 2026 paper identifies exact minimum all-symbol batch lengths as a motivating natural problem and leaves a one-column interval at k=t=4 for every odd finite field. The certificate closes this full infinite field family and determines both PIR and batch minima, rather than providing a small arbitrary numerical instance. A direct characteristic-independent resolution of a known parity-dependent construction is structurally informative even without a broader theorem.
